speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain; to ensure your safety, have you ever been diagnosed with an eating disorder or do you have a history of self-induced vomiting?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Esophageal Rupture). The patient's presentation of forceful vomiting following alcohol consumption, followed by severe chest pain and choking, is the classic triad for this life-threatening esophageal tear. Immediate surgical consultation and imaging (Chest X-Ray/CT) are required.
